nodes.label: SeaweedFS object storage
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Cloudflare R2 because activation demands a payment method the team decided not to register; the second custody barrier was lost

nodes.label: Nothing relevant is deleted
nodes.rationale: Addenda, replacements and report versions create new records; app_runtime has no DELETE on any table

nodes.rationale: Another project with admin access reaches this data; with real data the recommendation is a separate VPS

nodes.community_name: Isolado: Motion system (CSS tokens, no library)

nodes.label: Audit by database trigger with masked sensitive columns
nodes.norm_label: audit by database trigger with masked sensitive columns

nodes.label: Declarative drizzle/sql security layer
nodes.rationale: All policies and runtime grants are dropped and recreated in one transaction on each migration; drizzle-kit push is forbidden because it ignores them

nodes.label: Layered architecture (presentation, API, domain, persistence, database)
nodes.norm_label: layered architecture (presentation, api, domain, persistence, database)

nodes.label: Row Level Security on every table
nodes.norm_label: row level security on every table
nodes.rationale: Repositories do not filter by user: a defensive WHERE would hide a policy bug. FORCE RLS is not used because security definer functions and the audit trigger run as owner

nodes.label: withUser identity transaction wrapper
nodes.rationale: set_config must be transaction-local because the pool reuses connections; a session value would leak identity to another request

nodes.label: Write flow from Route Handler to audit trigger
nodes.norm_label: write flow from route handler to audit trigger

nodes.label: Manual migration rollback
nodes.rationale: Reverting is a manual decision, in reverse migration order, because it drops the tables and their data

nodes.label: Permission as intersection of profile and link
nodes.norm_label: permission as intersection of profile and link

nodes.label: Security model (RLS, three roles, audit triggers)
nodes.norm_label: security model (rls, three roles, audit triggers)
nodes.rationale: A query escaping the wrapper runs without identity and returns zero rows: a visible failure, not a silent one

nodes.label: Backup layers (pgBackRest, restic and rclone, Contabo Auto Backup)
nodes.norm_label: backup layers (pgbackrest, restic and rclone, contabo auto backup)

nodes.label: LUKS vault at /srv/dados
nodes.rationale: Docker does not start on boot on purpose: without the vault, containers would come back without their data

nodes.label: New server setup scripts (cofre-criar, publicar, configurar-deploy, backup-configurar)
nodes.norm_label: new server setup scripts (cofre-criar, publicar, configurar-deploy, backup-configurar)

nodes.label: Encrypted vault limited to 30% of the disk
nodes.norm_label: encrypted vault limited to 30% of the disk

nodes.label: SeaweedFS volumeSizeLimitMB=128
nodes.rationale: SeaweedFS reserves 7 volumes times the limit per bucket; the 1 GB default costs 7 GB per empty bucket

nodes.label: Shared server proxy at /srv/proxy
nodes.rationale: Docker ignores ufw, so containers publish no ports; only the proxy owns 80 and 443

nodes.label: Ask before reserving, deleting or resizing
nodes.norm_label: ask before reserving, deleting or resizing

nodes.label: Do not reserve disk just in case
nodes.norm_label: do not reserve disk just in case
nodes.rationale: The disk is shared: what one project reserves the others lose; growing is easy, shrinking takes the system down

nodes.label: Docker starts only after the vault opens
nodes.norm_label: docker starts only after the vault opens

nodes.label: Container memory ceilings (mem_limit, sum under 5 GB)
nodes.norm_label: container memory ceilings (mem_limit, sum under 5 gb)
nodes.rationale: 8 GB and no swap: an unbounded container can take down every project, and builds need about 2 GB outside containers

nodes.label: Roadmap phases 0-6
nodes.rationale: Order follows data dependency rather than RF numbering: without profile and link no RLS policy can be written

nodes.label: Local CI mirror (npm run ci, ci-local.mjs)
nodes.norm_label: local ci mirror (npm run ci, ci-local.mjs)

nodes.label: Environments (development, CI, production)
nodes.rationale: CI uses the same container and role script as local, so an RLS test passing locally passes in CI for the same reasons

nodes.label: Batch branch workflow (integration/<lote>)
nodes.rationale: develop never receives untested work: a batch is exhausted by the local CI before its PR, and only the PR runs remote CI

nodes.label: Three-layer flow guarantee (rulesets, remote CI, local hooks)
nodes.norm_label: three-layer flow guarantee (rulesets, remote ci, local hooks)
nodes.rationale: Local protections can be bypassed; the ruleset and PR CI cannot, so none of the layers depends on remembering the rule
